item.text:
**6B.9 Assessment: mostly no**

There are some real state programs with multi-year horizons, but the strongest 2024 evidence still points to centralized, personalized rule rather than durable social institutions that would clearly survive Putin.

| Orientation | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level note | Other IDs |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Supportive, weak | Universal free medical care program kept in force | Government of Russia | 2024-01-09 | https://government.ru/news/50600/ | A baseline health entitlement was preserved for 2024-2026, showing continuity in service delivery, but not institutional autonomy. | 6B.2, 6B.6, 6B.8 |
| Supportive, weak | `Zemsky Doctor` and `Zemsky Paramedic` extended through 2030 | Government of Russia | 2024-12-18 | https://government.ru/docs/53769/ | This is the best positive item: a multi-year staffing mechanism, compensation increases, and one-transfer flexibility suggest some institutionalization of rural health delivery. | 6B.2, 6B.4, 6B.5, 6B.9 |
| Supportive, weak | AI strategy amended through 2030 | Kremlin | 2024-02-15 | https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/50326/print | The decree expands datasets, open AI libraries, resilient networks, and civil-servant training, which is capacity-building, but it is state-directed rather than independently durable. | 6B.5, 6B.9 |
| Supportive, weak | Belousov appointed as defense minister | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-05-14 | https://theprint.in/world/belousov-says-russia-must-win-in-ukraine-while-minimising-troop-losses/2084728/ | Reuters framed this as technocratic professionalization and efficiency-seeking, but the same report ties it to war management and a loyalist security structure, so the institutional signal is limited. | 6B.4, 6B.5, 6B.9 |
| Negative, strong | Local autonomy, judiciary, and transparency remain hollow | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024 | Freedom House says autonomous local government ceased in 2020, the judiciary is heavily dependent on political discretion, and policymaking is centralized and opaque. That is strong evidence against durable institutions beyond Putin. | 6B.4, 6B.5, 6B.7, 6B.9 |
| Negative, strong | Putin widens secrecy privileges for economically significant entities | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-01-29 | https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-lets-economically-significant-entities-limit-information-disclosures-3315001 | Reducing disclosure weakens transparency and outside scrutiny, which makes institutional durability and correction after Putin less likely. | 6B.5, 6B.7, 6B.9 |
| Negative, strong | Russia: repressive laws used to crush civic freedoms | Human Rights Watch | 2024-08-07 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/07/russia-repressive-laws-used-crush-civic-freedoms | HRW says hundreds have been jailed under repressive laws and civil society has been pushed into exile or underground, which is the opposite of building resilient, self-sustaining civic institutions. | 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.9 |

Search gap: I found no solid 2024 evidence that Putin built genuinely autonomous courts, local governments, unions, or civic organizations that could outlast him. The positive evidence is mostly centralized administrative programming with fixed end dates; the negative evidence is about concentration of power, opacity, and repression.
